paper_title: Prometheus 2 An Open Source Language Model Specialized in Evaluating   Other Language Models
caption: When merging models, the influence of relative evaluation on absolute evaluation is greater than the influence of absolute evaluation on relative evaluation. Performance of Direct Assessment (colored in green) and Pairwise Ranking (colored in blue) when altering the value to merge evaluator LMs trained on different formats.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the performance of two evaluation methods—Direct Assessment (green line) and Pairwise Ranking (blue line)—as well as their average performance (black line) when merging language models trained on different formats, with the x-axis representing the (Direct Assessment : Pairwise Ranking) Merging Ratio ranging from 1.9 to 9.1 on a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of approximately 0.9. The left y-axis, labeled "Direct Assessment Pearson Correlation," ranges from 0.500 to 0.675 with increments of 0.025, and the right y-axis, labeled "Pairwise Ranking Agreement Accuracy," ranges from 50 to 80 with increments of 5. The green line (Direct Assessment Correlation) starts at approximately 0.500 at a merging ratio of 1.9, rises steadily to a peak of about 0.670 at 5.5, and then declines to around 0.580 at 9.1. The blue line (Pairwise Ranking Accuracy) begins at approximately 0.660 at 1.9, increases slightly to about 0.675 at 3.7, then gradually decreases to around 0.500 at 9.1. The black line (Average Performance) starts at about 0.575 at 1.9, increases to a peak of approximately 0.610 at 5.5, and then decreases to roughly 0.530 at 9.1.
